title: Mediterranean Cypress: Ancient Cypresses You Can Visit
meta_description: The dark exclamation mark of the Mediterranean, planted for mourning and memory for 3,000 years. The oldest cypresses mapped so far, cemeteries included.
intro: The Mediterranean cypress is the most recognisable punctuation mark in landscape: a dark green exclamation point that Van Gogh painted obsessively and that Greeks, Romans and Persians planted at graves for three thousand years before him. The mourning association is practical as much as poetic, because the tree is close to immortal by garden standards, evergreen, drought-proof and content on thin stony soil, exactly the qualities you want from something meant to outlast grief. Its species name sempervirens simply means always alive. Individual cypresses in Iran are credibly claimed at four thousand years. The cypresses mapped so far stand in cemeteries, monastery courtyards and old gardens, oldest first.
